attachments.origin_landmark: posterior nasal spine and the palatine aponeurosis (bilateral; a single bone is named because the schema takes one origin)
attachments.insertion_landmark: mucosa of the uvula (bilateral bellies fused across the midline)

actions: shortens and thickens the uvula, helping seal the nasopharynx

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Paired bellies fused across the midline. Deviation of the uvula AWAY from the side of a vagal lesion is the classic bedside sign, because the intact side pulls unopposed.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Not an ultrasound-guided technique -- injected transorally, under direct visualization (not EMG or imaging guidance), placed medially on either side of the uvula. Used for palatal myoclonus/tremor when the predominant presenting symptom is patient-perceived palatal movement (rather than clicking tinnitus, for which tensor veli palatini is instead the initial target).
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: Direct visualization of rhythmic uvula/soft palate movement on oral exam; dose and site of subsequent injections are tailored to the location of the maximal observed muscular contraction on follow-up.
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Palatal myoclonus (essential or secondary, e.g. post-viral) is the only indication found; it is a rare movement disorder, not a mainstream BoNT target. An older case report also describes transoral BoNT injection into the soft palate/uvula region for palatal myoclonus with objective tinnitus. Dosing was individualized/titrated rather than fixed.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Sinclair CF, Gurey LE, Blitzer A, 'Palatal myoclonus: algorithm for management with botulinum toxin based on clinical disease characteristics', Laryngoscope 124(5):1164-1169 (2014), doi:10.1002/lary.23485 -- retrieved via PubMed; Varney SM, Demetroulakos JL, Fletcher MH, McQueen WJ, Hamilton MK, 'Palatal myoclonus: treatment with Clostridium botulinum toxin injection', Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 114(2):317-320 (1996), doi:10.1016/S0194-59989670194-8 -- retrieved via PubMed.
